crates/reflow2-core/tests/unverified_published_contract.rs.

SIX PROBES: a published contract with no check is named and an internal one never is; a PASSING check settles it while a `planned` one does not (`dec:passing-is-verified`); `both` is billed and `required` is not; publishing nothing raises the posture question instead of reading clean, and stands down the moment somebody designates a boundary; a design with no boundaries at all is asked nothing; and the posture question keeps one id as the population moves while each contract gets its own.

EIGHT MUTATIONS RUN. Six killed by exactly their own probe: bill `required`; bill `internal`; drop `both`; let any attached check silence it; drop the posture finding so publishing nothing reads clean; make the per-contract finding aggregate so two contracts collapse into one question.

🛑 TWO SURVIVED, AND BOTH WERE WORTH MORE THAN THE SIX THAT DIED.

  (1) BILLING `required` SURVIVED THE FIRST ROUND, AND THAT WAS A REAL TEST DEFECT. The probe read ONE finding's `affected_ids` and asserted `required` was absent — but this detector emits one finding PER CONTRACT, so the mutation simply added a SECOND finding and the first still looked right. An inert assertion of exactly the class caught earlier the same day in the vocabulary work. Fixed by asking what the detector billed ACROSS ALL findings, which is the only question that can see it; the mutation then died.

  (2) FLIPPING `NoPublishedBoundary` OFF THE AGGREGATE LIST STILL SURVIVES, AND THAT IS NOT A WEAK TEST. `gap_id` short-circuits on `is_aggregate`, but the per-node branch hashes the affected list — and this finding names NO nodes, so the id is stable either way. The declaration is therefore unobservable today. It is kept at `true` because it states what the finding IS, and because it becomes load-bearing the moment anyone gives it `affected_ids` — and both the source and the test say so in words, so a reader does not mistake it for protection being exercised. Same shape as the dead guard mutation exposed in `detect_internal_only_delivery`.

RUN AGAINST REFLOW2'S OWN DESIGN through the built binary: 3 published boundaries, 2 findings — `ifc:graph-export` and `ifc:mcp-tools-http`, each with 0 incoming VERIFIES — and `ifc:mcp-tools` silent because it carries a passing check. Gaps 73 to 75.

⚠️ THE FIRST RUN AGAINST THE REAL DESIGN SHOWED NOTHING, and the detector was fine: `reflow2_check.py` prefers `target/debug/reflow2-mcp` and only the release binary had been rebuilt. A green gate over a stale binary is the same trap as a stale MCP server, one tool over.
properties.findings: 6 probes pass. Whole workspace green (exit 0, both crates). Against reflow2's own design through the built binary: 3 boundaries designated published, 2 reported — `ifc:graph-export` and `ifc:mcp-tools-http`, each 0 incoming VERIFIES — and `ifc:mcp-tools` silent because it carries a passing check. Design-wide gaps 73 to 75, and `no_published_boundary` correctly does NOT fire here because this design does publish something. 8 mutations run, 6 killed; the 2 survivors are recorded in the description rather than hidden, and one of them was a real defect in a probe that has since been fixed.
properties.name: Six probes over both findings, and the two mutations that survived are recorded rather than hidden
